title: Food: supplies, cooking and safety
short: Supplies, cooking without power, what to throw away
intro: Readings on keeping food at home for a week or more, cooking when the electric stove is off, and knowing when food is no longer safe to eat.

limits.text: Indoors, cook only with devices approved for indoor use; camping stoves and grills belong outside.
Carbon monoxide poisoning can kill, and an open fire indoors can cause it too.
Throw away a tin whose lid bulges outwards.
Throw away nuts that taste odd or show mould, and meat that is slimy or smells strong.
Do not eat food that touched flood water: it may be contaminated.
